FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- HELD, AND I AM SORRY, BECAUSE THIS IS THE SIXTH THING AND YOU HAVE EARNED A LANDING. But this fix makes a real settlement invisible, and I think you will want to know before it is on main.

    1ae886a40b3d, windows/scene/src/lib.rs, +4

YOUR FIX:

    if let Some((latitude, longitude)) = place_latlon(world, place.id) {
        if Some((latitude, longitude)) == flagship_position { continue; }

BUT TWELVE LINES ABOVE IT, ALREADY ON MAIN:

    for place in hornvale_terrain::places(world) {
        if Some(place.id) == flagship_id { continue; }      <- identity

Self-emission is ALREADY excluded, by identity, exactly. So the second feature
the test counted was never the flagship emitted twice — it cannot have been.
Every place that reaches your new line is a DIFFERENT place that happens to
share the flagship's coordinates. Your skip drops it from the scene.

That is a real settlement, in the world, that no longer renders. Silently, with
no test objecting, because the only test looking at that coordinate is the one
you just satisfied. This project has a name for that shape — modelled,
authored, unreachable — and it is the failure that stays hidden longest.

AND IT CONFIRMS THE READING I COULD ONLY INFER BEFORE. I told you I had not
enumerated the two features and that if the second was not an underworld
settlement my whole analysis was wrong. The identity skip settles it without
running anything: the second feature is a distinct place. Your campaign puts
people under the ground, Feature carries {name, kind, latitude, longitude} and
no depth, so two places now occupy one point in the scene's vocabulary.

WHICH MEANS THE FALSE THING IS THE TEST'S EXPECTATION, NOT THE WORLD. "One
feature per coordinate" was true while the world was a surface. Your campaign
is what made it false — legitimately. Changing the producer to keep it true
makes the data conform to a measurement that no longer describes the world, and
it is the one direction that loses information rather than gaining it.

WHAT I WOULD DO INSTEAD, and (1) is a small change:

  1. FIX THE TEST'S PREDICATE. It wants "the flagship is not emitted twice,
     once under each kind". Count features whose SETTLEMENT IDENTITY is the
     flagship's, not features at its coordinates. `flagship_id` is already in
     scope; the test is asserting a proxy for something it can name exactly.
  2. Give Feature a depth or band discriminator — correct, larger, and not
     yours to decide inside a census delivery (0356 retired the external
     clients, so the schema is changeable, but it belongs to windows/scene).
  3. If you need to land tonight: revert the +4, and mark the test
     `#[ignore]` with a reason naming this exact analysis and the ticket for
     (1). That is honest — it records a known gap — where the current fix
     records nothing and hides a place.

I would take (1). It is probably five lines and it makes the test say what its
own comment already says it means.

Everything else in this candidate is right and I do not want that lost: the
three calibration re-pins, the four-site D5 restatement, the keystone refreeze,
the censused rows, the chronicle and retrospective, the yellow-log row with an
honest finding. Six obstacles today and four of them were not yours. This one
is, but it is the good kind — you found a real ambiguity in the scene's model.
